title: Call contract orchestration: provenance-aware parameter grammar and heuristic repair
creator: Marina Alvarez
description:
Goal: Define a pragmatic JSON schema/mini-grammar and a multi-stage validation orchestration for function/tool calls that preserves provenance, supports backward-compatible shims, and surfaces human-friendly repair hints when inputs are ambiguous or mal-typed.

Background: Current runtime validations are brittle for real prompts: users often pass values with minor variations, missing optional fields, or ambiguous enums. We need an orchestration layer that can run conservative checks first, then a provenance-aware coercion and ambiguity resolution pass, and finally return structured diagnostics and repair suggestions. This ticket specifies the format, error taxonomy, compatibility modes, telemetry, and rollout plan.

Key principles: 1) Preserve origin metadata for every parameter (where it came from: user prompt, client SDK default, inferred by shim) so we can display explanations and compute repair trust scores. 2) Fail closed in strict mode for enterprise customers (strict compatibility for Private/Dedicated), but provide a tolerant mode for Hosted/PLG to reduce friction. 3) Return actionable, localized suggestions for fixable problems (example: candidate resolutions for ambiguous enums, type coercion suggestions with confidence). 4) Keep the runtime impact small: fast shallow checks, async heavier repairs where possible, and telemetry to measure false-correct rates.

Proposed JSON profile format (human summary): a compact contract block per function describing fields, short canonical type, allowed aliases, canonicalizers, and a provenance policy. Example fields described as text: name, type, required, aliases, canonicalizer (label of a canonicalization routine), enum_candidates, fallback_strategy (shim, default, reject), human_hint.

Validation orchestration stages (summary):
- Stage 0: Shallow shape check (presence, basic JSON types) -> fast reject if missing required in strict mode.
- Stage 1: Alias resolution & canonicalization (apply canonicalizers; track provenance if value changed).
- Stage 2: Ambiguity scoring (for enums, ambiguous free-text, and structural unions) -> produce ranked candidates with confidence scores.
- Stage 3: Heuristic repair attempt (if mode == tolerant and candidate confidence >= threshold) -> return repaired object and a diagnostic envelope describing what changed.
- Stage 4: Final acceptance or rejection with structured error codes and user-friendly messages.

Error taxonomy (sample error codes and human messages):
- ERR-PARAM-MISSING: required parameter missing. Human: "Missing required field 'destination' for 'route' tool."
- ERR-PARAM-TYPE: type mismatch that cannot be coerced. Human: "Expected number for 'timeout' but got 'five minutes'."
- ERR-PARAM-COERCED: value coerced with provenance note. Human: "Interpreted '5m' as integer 300 for 'timeout' (source: client-default)."
- ERR-PARAM-AMBIGUOUS: multiple valid candidates discovered. Human: "Multiple matches for 'size': Small, Medium, Large. Defaulting to 'Medium' — confirm if incorrect."
- ERR-PARAM-REPAIRED: repair applied; diagnostic includes original value and repair confidence. Human: "Auto-corrected 'janury' -> 'January' with 0.85 confidence."

Suggested diagnostic envelope returned in API (described in prose): a top-level diagnostics array of short objects containing code, field path, short message, suggested_fix (text), confidence (0-1), provenance_chain (list of provenance tags), and a human_facing_hint. The runtime will also attach a compact summary header for SDKs and a verbose blob accessible from the Console.

Compatibility & shim policies:
- Strict: enterprise default. No automated repairs. Any deviation returns an error.
- Tolerant: Hosted default. Repairs allowed up to a configurable confidence threshold per customer (default 0.75). Repairs are recorded and surfaced.
- Shim: For legacy clients we provide opt-in shims that map deprecated field names/structures to the canonical contract with explicit provenance tagged as 'shim'.

Telemetry and SLOs: capture metrics per-call: validation_latency_ms, repairs_applied_count, repair_confidence_histogram, param_repair_rate_by_field, false_repair_rate_estimate (based on post-call confirmations), and customer_override_rate. Target: keep added median validation latency < 3ms in hot path; run more expensive heuristics only when needed and asynchronously in the request lifecycle where possible.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement contract schema parser and shallow checks behind feature flag. 2) Add canonicalizers and alias maps for top 20 most-used tools. 3) Pilot tolerant repair logic for non-critical tools and only for internal beta customers. 4) Monitor telemetry for false repair > 2% and rollback repairs for fields exceeding threshold. 5) Expose diagnostics in Console and create an SDK option to surface repair suggestions to product teams.

Acceptance criteria:
- Spec doc describing contract block and diagnostic envelope committed to Confluence (link in comments).
- Implementation of staged orchestration + unit tests covering ambiguity/repair cases.
- Pilot enabled for 3 tools with telemetry showing repair precision >= 0.80 for those tools.

Migration notes: existing tool manifests will be auto-mapped to new compact contract format using shim rules; devs must review auto-generated alias maps and sign off during the pilot.

Open questions: how to represent nested provenance for arrays of objects without increasing envelope size? Should we allow a per-field confidence override via customer config? These are tracked in comments below.
